What this page practises

  • I can state that the mass of a galaxy is estimated from the orbital speed of its stars.
  • I can explain how galaxy mass estimates give evidence for dark matter.
  • I can state that the accelerating expansion gives evidence for dark energy.
  • I can state that gravity works against the expansion.

Answers

Say it the exam way

(1) orbital speed · (2) larger · (3) matter · (4) against · (5) increasing · (6) energy

2022 Paper 1, Question 8: answer D

  • A Not this one. I is correct, but II is correct too: the accelerating expansion is the evidence for dark energy.
  • B Not this one. II is correct, but I is too: dark matter comes from estimates of the mass of galaxies.
  • C Not this one. III is wrong. Hotter stars peak at a shorter wavelength, not a longer one. You meet this in Part 4.
  • D Right. I and II match the evidence for dark matter and dark energy. III is wrong: hotter stars peak at a shorter wavelength. You meet this in Part 4.
  • E Not this one. I and II are correct, but III is wrong. Hotter stars peak at a shorter wavelength (Part 4).

2019 Paper 1, Question 10: answer E

  • A Not this one. I is correct, but it is not the only one. Check II and III against your notes on dark energy and dark matter.
  • B Not this one. II is correct, but so are the others. Gravity does pull against the expansion.
  • C Not this one. III is correct: that is how a galaxy's mass is estimated. But I and II are correct too.
  • D Not this one. I and II are correct, but so is III. The orbital speed of the stars is how a galaxy's mass is estimated.
  • E Right. I: gravity pulls against the expansion. II: the rate of expansion is increasing, the evidence for dark energy. III: a galaxy's mass is estimated from the orbital speed of its stars.

2017 Section 1, Question 6: answer C

  • A Not this one. Redshift is how we measure that galaxies move away. It is evidence for the expansion, not its cause.
  • B Not this one. Dark matter comes from estimates of galaxy mass. Its gravity would slow the expansion, not speed it up.
  • C Right. An increasing rate of expansion is the evidence for dark energy.
  • D Not this one. Gravity acts against the expansion. On its own it would slow the expansion down.
  • E Not this one. The cosmic microwave background is evidence for the Big Bang. It does not explain why the expansion is speeding up.

2018 Section 2, Question 5(c)
